THE EDITOR’S SELECTION

Eight sources. Eight useful roles.

A focused starting shelf chosen for visual specificity, useful context and a clear role in the research process. These are editorial choices, not a ranking; access notes remain in the directory.

Arrange your selected references on a focused local canvas for a shoot or design brief.

CHOOSE YOUR NEXT PROJECT

Start with a purpose.

Four reading routes turn discovery into a concrete deliverable. Open a route, follow its three steps, then keep your references with context.

01Prepare a photo shootTranslate a mood into a usable brief.+

  1. Define the story

    The Gentlewoman ↗ · SHOWstudio ↗

    Choose a portrait mood, lighting direction and movement reference.

  2. Study the outfit

    FASHIONSNAP ↗ · Vogue Runway ↗

    Annotate silhouette, proportion and styling details from dated examples.

  3. Build the brief

    PureRef ↗ · Milanote ↗

    Group references into light, wardrobe, location and poses; add credits and a shot list.

Your outcome
A concise shoot brief with a credited board and a shot list.

02Research Asian fashionCompare sources within each market.+

  1. Choose the market

    Vogue China ↗ · Vogue Korea ↗ · FASHIONSNAP ↗

    Start with one country, city or styling question.

  2. Compare the evidence

    MUSINSA Snap ↗ · Tokyo Fashion ↗ · Jing Daily ↗

    Separate daily outfits, archived street photography and market reporting; check dates.

  3. Keep the source trail

    Are.na ↗ · Raindrop.io ↗

    Save original links and explain what each reference contributes.

Your outcome
A dated comparison board with country, source type and styling notes.

03Design a magazineDevelop a consistent editorial system.+

  1. Study the editorial rhythm

    The Gentlewoman ↗ · Apartamento ↗

    Compare opening spreads, portrait pacing and relationships between text and images.

  2. Explore the design language

    Magazine B ↗ · Behance ↗

    Annotate grids, hierarchy, captions and image scale rather than copying a complete layout.

  3. Organize the direction

    Are.na ↗ · Milanote ↗

    Create a type, palette and layout board, then sketch your own opening spread.

Your outcome
A visual style sheet and an original spread concept.

04Identify vintage garmentsBuild an attribution from several clues.+

  1. Record the object

    Vintage Fashion Guild ↗

    Document labels, seams, fabric and construction before assigning a date.

  2. Compare historical context

    FIT Fashion History Timeline ↗ · Kyoto Costume Institute ↗

    Check documented silhouettes and object dates; similarities are leads, not proof.

  3. Trace the image

    TinEye ↗ · Wayback Machine ↗

    Investigate matching images and historical pages; keep the source record and uncertainty.

Your outcome
An object record with evidence, a provisional date range and unresolved questions.

03 / FROM DISCOVERY TO DIRECTION

Build a board with a purpose.

  1. Define the visual question

    Choose one subject per board: a silhouette, fabric, styling detail, palette or page treatment.

  2. Collect with context

    Save the original page or creator post, image credit, publication date, country/city, and the styling detail you want to study.

  3. Compare references

    Use several independent examples. Keep runway, street photography, product listings, historical objects and AI interpretations visibly separate.

  4. Build the board

    Group by silhouette, material, palette and accessory. Add a sentence explaining each selection instead of collecting lookalikes without context.

  5. Keep the final record in Obsidian

    Store permitted local copies with the source record; revisit the original page before publication. A collection link alone is not a durable backup.

04 / THE RESEARCH RECORD

Keep the context.

One record for each reference.

Use this structure in Obsidian or your bookmark manager. A useful board explains what each image contributes.

Why this reference matters

Access & publication.

Source links do not grant image reproduction rights. Record the individual item’s terms or permission status before magazine publication. Login flows, paid features, offline saving and native apps were not tested.

What changed from the first list.

We Heart It stays a legacy lead: its retrieved public page did not expose a usable discovery interface. This does not establish the status of every app or account feature.

Are.na does not guarantee that external sources will remain available. Dewu and Xiaohongshu are useful leads, but the earlier “best” rankings were unsupported. Shaarli’s GitHub page is retained; the earlier certificate claim was not rechecked.

Search in the source language.

China: 新中式穿搭 · 马面裙穿搭
Japan: ストリートスナップ · 古着 コーデ
Korea: 데일리룩 · 아쿠비 · 한복 스타일링

Suggested search phrases, not measured trend rankings.

05 / A WIDER READING PRACTICE

Read the fashion landscape.

Combine visual inspiration with the context needed to interpret it.

  1. Editorial direction

    Read i-D, The Gentlewoman or System for photography, styling and the editorial argument.

  2. Market context

    Use Luxe.CO, Business of Fashion or FashionNetwork to investigate the business behind a visual signal.

  3. Community signals

    Compare dated creator posts, outfit discussions and resale listings; avoid universal trend claims.

  4. Historical grounding

    Use KCI, FIT and the Vintage Fashion Guild to distinguish a revival from a new silhouette.

  5. Trace and monitor

    Trace image matches with TinEye, check historical captures and monitor available feeds with Inoreader.

Review sources weekly and synthesize monthly. Label editorial, market, community and historical evidence; record season and look identifiers when available.

Selected additions informed by your supplied fashion-media report. Unverified prices, leadership and ownership claims, audience counts and blanket free-access claims were omitted.

RESEARCH EDITION / 2026-10-13 · This directory works offline; external sources require internet. No accounts created or services connected. Links lead to official sources; each reference needs its own date, credit and context.
